Hi Lauren,

Quick note — we hit an unexpected burst last Thursday during a product demo wave and our response latency climbed into the 600–900ms range for ~18 minutes. Ops attached the 05/2028 usage slice so you can see the spike pattern. Our renewal is coming up 2028-07-01 and the team is nervous about guaranteeing the same performance if we stay on the current commit.

A few asks:
- Can Redwood provide a short-term burst/top-up option to cover spikes through the renewal?
- We'd like a sizing recommendation (how many GPUs and what instance types) that balances cost + 99th percentile latency target of <400ms for our critical routes.
- If we agree on a temporary top-up, can it be added into the renewal as a staged commit so we don’t overspend?

We can share access to more logs if needed. We appreciate a quick turnaround — can we have a proposal by early next week?

Thanks,
Florian Bouchard

Hi Florian — thanks for the heads-up and for sending the usage slice.

Short answer: yes, we can do a short-term burst/top-up and fold a staged commitment into the renewal so the spend is predictable. I skimmed the CSV and saw two characteristics that matter for sizing: the spike is short (~18m) but very high concurrency, and your 95th/99th tail comes from a small subset of routes with long sequences.

Proposed interim plan (quick summary):
- Immediate: add an 8-GPU burst pool (NVIDIA A100-equivalent) dedicated to your critical routes for the next 6 weeks. This should reduce 99th-percentile latency below 400ms in our tests.
- Observability: we'll enable per-route token-level tracing for the burst pool and provide daily snapshots to your ops team.
- Cost path: treat the 8-GPU as a time-boxed burst charge for June + half of July; if you choose to make it permanent in the renewal, we convert to a staged commit with a 3-month ramp clause.
- Next step: Ben (copied) will validate the sizing and confirm autoscaling/burst limits; once agreed we'll attach an amendment to the SOW and provide a DocuSign link.

I've attached an initial SOW draft outlining the staging language and conversion mechanics. Does the timeline below work?
- Proposal + Sizing: by EOD Mon 2028-06-05
- Implementation (if approved): 48–72 hours from sign-off

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Fwd: Capacity hiccup last week + renewal timeline — quick sizing ask

Ben / Vivek — forwarding NimbleCare's note (below). They saw a short high-concurrency spike and asked for an interim burst top-up ahead of a renewal on 2028-07-01. I proposed an 8-GPU A100-equivalent burst pool for 6 weeks with staged conversion at renewal, but want your quick input before I send formal numbers.

Key context:
- Critical routes have long sequences; average token lengths 120–200, but peak sequences hit ~600 tokens during the demo flows (see CSV).
- Baseline commit today is 24 GPUs; their average sustained utilization is ~60% but tail usage pushes them into saturation for brief windows.
- Pricing sensitivity: they asked to cap incremental monthly spend; they'd prefer staged commit conversion vs. an immediate permanent top-up.

Questions for Ben:
1) Is 8 A100-equivalent GPUs the right ballpark to get 99th <400ms given those sequence lengths and a mix of batching + cache? If not, what delta?
2) Any quick notes on kernel/quantization profile changes we'd recommend so they don't regress quality with the burst pool?

Vivek — if we greenlight this, would you recommend folding the staged commit into the renewal as a month-over-month ramp (e.g., 2/4/6 GPUs over 3 months) or convert to a fixed add-on? The customer prefers predictable spend.

Please reply with bullets; I'll synthesize and send back to Florian Monday.

Thanks,
Lauren

Hi Lauren / Ben — thanks for the quick work on sizing and the call last week. We reviewed the numbers with Finance and Ops. Proposed adjustments below and next steps: 

Agreed interim plan:
- Approve a staged 6-week burst: 6 GPUs live in week 1, 8 GPUs in weeks 2–5, then 4 GPUs as a standing short-term buffer in week 6 while we finalize the renewal language.
- Cap on incremental monthly spend for the burst: $14,500 (we can't exceed this without additional approvals).
- If performance meets the target (99th <400ms) for the evaluation window, we will convert to a 4-GPU permanent add-on in the renewal with a 3-month ramp clause.

Requests / small redlines:
- Please add a clause that the staged burst will be billed as a distinct line item and that conversion to permanent commit requires a signed amendment (DocuSign).
- Can Redwood guarantee no model changes that materially affect latency during the evaluation window (we understand you may need minor kernel updates; please notify us in advance)?

I've attached a lightly-redlined SOW (v2) and included a DocuSign link to expedite the amendment once we align on exact GPU counts/dates. If the above is acceptable, we can sign and you can spin up the first tranche next Monday.

Thanks,
Florian Bouchard
